reference: GNU rsync (the system rsync executable invoked by reference Bash with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin) is the independent oracle for local-copy behavior. The metadata contract is grounded in Bash's type/help interface and the rsync documentation. No candidate-produced output is used as an expectation.
coverage: Single-file destination selection and byte copying
Multiple source files mapped into a new destination directory
Recursive archive copy with permissions and a relative symlink
Source trailing-slash mapping of directory contents
Dry-run leaves a missing destination absent
--delete removes destination entries absent from the source
Partial source failure returns rsync status 23 while copying surviving sources
Default transfer preserves an existing destination file mode
Bash type/help metadata for the rsync builtin
exclusions: Remote rsh/SSH push and pull require a disposable peer or transport mock; no network activity is performed.
Native protocol and rsync daemon transfers require a disposable rsync server/mock and are not executed.
This suite does not qualify delta/compression wire transfers, hard-link preservation, ACLs, xattrs, special files, nanosecond mtime preservation, or atomic-write interruption behavior.

cases.purpose: Confirm builtin registration and the documented one-line description using Bash help -d; the first line of full help is a synopsis header.
cases.stdout:
builtin
rsync - Minimal rsync subset: push, pull, native proto-27 and daemon transfers.

cases.purpose: A single source file copied to a missing destination without a slash is a file at that exact path, as GNU rsync specifies.
cases.script:
printf 'small fixture\n' > source
rsync source copied

cases.purpose: Multiple source files make a missing destination a directory even without a trailing slash, with each file retaining its basename.
cases.script:
printf 'first\n' > one
printf 'second\n' > two
rsync -a one two bundle

cases.purpose: Archive mode recursively copies a directory tree, preserves a non-default file mode, and recreates a relative symlink with the same target.
cases.script:
mkdir -p src/nested
printf 'payload\n' > src/nested/file
chmod 640 src/nested/file
ln -s nested/file src/link
rsync -a src dest/

cases.purpose: A trailing slash on a recursive source copies the directory contents directly into the destination instead of adding the source directory basename.
cases.script:
mkdir -p src/sub
printf 'top\n' > src/top
printf 'nested\n' > src/sub/inner
rsync -r src/ out

cases.purpose: Archive dry-run on a contents-style source reports success without creating the absent destination or changing the fixture tree.
cases.script:
mkdir -p src/sub
printf 'dry run\n' > src/sub/file
rsync -an src/ absent

cases.purpose: With --delete, syncing source directory contents removes stale files at both the destination root and a nested directory while retaining source entries.
cases.script:
mkdir -p src/sub dest/sub
printf 'keep\n' > src/sub/keep
printf 'stale\n' > dest/stale
printf 'extra\n' > dest/sub/extra
rsync -a --delete src/ dest/

cases.purpose: GNU rsync returns status 23 for a missing source while still transferring a surviving source; capture that command status and verify the copied tree.
cases.script:
printf 'surviving input\n' > good
rc=0
rsync -a missing good dest/ || rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 23 ]
printf 'rsync-status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: When default rsync replaces an existing file without -p, GNU rsync retains the destination's existing mode.
cases.script:
printf 'new payload\n' > source
printf 'old\n' > target
chmod 600 target
rsync source target

cases.purpose: Exercise remote push and pull through an rsh command using a disposable transport peer.
Exercise rsync --native interoperability against a disposable stock rsync server process.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r2: The destination tree matches, but the candidate-side stock sender exits 12 while the candidate reports success; a clean native peer completion is not established.; r3: Not executed.

cases.purpose: Exercise rsync daemon URL/module transfers against a disposable rsync daemon mock.
cases.reason: No executed fixture runs an rsync daemon. A per-side script can background the trusted /usr/bin/rsync --daemon on 127.0.0.1 with a private config.

cases.purpose: An empty source directory still creates the requested private destination directory.
cases.script:
mkdir src
rsync -a src/ dest/
[[ -d dest ]]
